concept.body: To classify a triangle by its sides, compare the LONGEST side's square c² with the sum of the other two squares a² + b². Equal → right. c² smaller → acute (the long side is too short to open a 90° angle). c² larger → obtuse.

check.body: Which way does the comparison point?
explanationVariants: c² = 100 versus 36 + 49 = 85: c² is larger, so the biggest angle passes 90° — obtuse.
100 > 85 means the longest side stretches its opposite angle open: obtuse.

options.label: Obtuse — 100 > 36 + 49 = 85
options.feedback: The longest square beats the other two combined, so the opposite angle exceeds 90°.

options.label: Acute — 100 is a nice round number
Right — 6² + 8² = 10²
options.feedback: The middle side here is 7, not 8: 36 + 49 = 85 ≠ 100 → obtuse.

steps.body: The theorem runs in reverse. **Converse:** if a triangle's sides satisfy a² + b² = c² (c the longest), the angle opposite c is exactly 90° — the triangle is right. No protractor needed: three side lengths alone certify a right angle. Builders' “3-4-5 rope trick” for square corners is this converse at work.
The converse, run backwards from the sides.

widget.prompt: Two sides of 6 and 8. Set the third side so the angle between the first two is exactly 90°.
widget.successFeedback: A third side of 10: 6² + 8² = 100 = 10². The converse of Pythagoras is exactly this reading — if the three sides satisfy the equation, the angle MUST be right. Shorten the third side and the angle closes to acute; lengthen it and it opens to obtuse. The sides decide the angle.
widget.lowFeedback: The angle is still under 90° — the third side is too short, pulling the other two together.
widget.highFeedback: The angle has passed 90° — the third side is too long, forcing them apart.

predict.prompt: Sides 6 and 8: which third side makes the angle between them exactly 90°?
predict.reveal: The converse runs Pythagoras backwards: if the third side satisfies c² = 6² + 8² = 100, the angle MUST be right. Shorter than 10 squeezes it acute; longer pries it obtuse — the third side is an angle gauge.

cml.actionGoal: Vary a triangle side or angle and connect the visible shape to the law of cosines.

explanationVariants: 8² + 15² = 64 + 225 = 289 = 17² — the equation balances, so the triangle is right.
Compare the longest side's square (289) with the sum of the other two (64 + 225 = 289): equal → right.

widget.prompt: Sides 8, 15, 17. Right triangle or not — and what's the test?

options.label: Right: 64 + 225 = 289 = 17²
options.feedback: Sum of the two smaller squares equals the largest square — converse says right angle opposite 17.

options.label: Not right: 8 + 15 = 23 ≠ 17
options.feedback: Adding sides tests nothing. Square first: 64 + 225 = 289 = 17² — it IS right.

options.label: Right: 17 − 15 = 2 and 8 ÷ 2 = 4
options.feedback: That arithmetic isn't the theorem. The genuine test: 64 + 225 = 289 = 17² — right, but for the Pythagorean reason.

options.label: Not right: 289 is odd... uneven squares can't balance
options.feedback: Parity is irrelevant — the squares balance exactly: 64 + 225 = 289 = 17², so it's right.

steps.body: When the equation does NOT balance, the imbalance tells you the triangle's type. Compare c² (longest side squared) against a² + b²: **c² = a² + b² → right. c² < a² + b² → acute** (the long side is too short to force 90°). **c² > a² + b² → obtuse** (the long side stretches the angle past 90°).

widget.prompt: Sides 6, 7, 9. Compute 6² + 7² = 85 and 9² = 81. The triangle is…

options.label: Acute — c² = 81 is LESS than 85
options.feedback: The longest side's square falls short of the other two, so the biggest angle stays under 90°: acute.

options.label: Obtuse — 85 is bigger, and bigger means obtuse
options.feedback: Read the comparison from c²'s side: c² = 81 < 85 = a² + b² means the big angle is squeezed BELOW 90° — acute.

options.label: Right — 81 and 85 are close enough
options.feedback: Right requires exact equality. 81 ≠ 85, and 81 < 85 lands it on the acute side.

options.label: Impossible — no triangle has these sides
options.feedback: 6 + 7 = 13 > 9, so the triangle exists. And since 81 < 85, it's acute.

explanationVariants: 4² + 7² = 65 while 9² = 81; since c² > a² + b², the angle opposite 9 exceeds 90°: obtuse.
The longest side's square (81) beats the other two combined (65) — the long side stretches the angle open: obtuse.

options.label: Obtuse — 81 > 16 + 49 = 65
options.feedback: c² exceeds a² + b², so the angle opposite the 9 opens past 90°.

options.label: Acute — all sides are under 10
options.feedback: Absolute size never decides type; the comparison does. 81 > 65 → obtuse.

options.label: Right — 4-7-9 is a Pythagorean triple
options.feedback: Check: 16 + 49 = 65 ≠ 81. Not a triple, and since 81 > 65, it's obtuse.

options.label: Equilateral — the sides are roughly equal
options.feedback: Equilateral needs sides exactly equal (4 ≠ 7 ≠ 9). The square test gives 81 > 65: obtuse.

steps.body: Whole-number side sets that balance exactly — like 3-4-5, 5-12-13, 8-15-17, 7-24-25 — are **Pythagorean triples**. Any multiple of a triple is a triple too: 3-4-5 scales to 6-8-10, 9-12-15, 30-40-50. Recognizing them turns square-root work into instant recall.

explanationVariants: 6-8-10 is 3-4-5 doubled, so the hypotenuse of legs 6, 8 is 10 — already verified earlier by direct computation.

widget.prompt: Legs 30 and 40 — use a scaled triple to name the hypotenuse instantly.

commonErrors.feedback: 70 = 30 + 40 adds legs. This is 3-4-5 scaled by 10, so c = 50 (900 + 1600 = 2500).

hints: Square the two smaller sides and add: 20² + 21².
explanationVariants: 400 + 441 = 841 = 29² exactly, so by the converse the triangle is right.
The sum of the smaller squares equals the largest square (841 = 841): right triangle, and 20-21-29 is a genuine triple.

widget.prompt: A triangle has sides 20, 21, 29. What's the verdict?

options.label: Right — 400 + 441 = 841 = 29²
options.feedback: Exact balance certifies the right angle: 20-21-29 is a Pythagorean triple.

options.label: Obtuse — 29 is much longer than 20 and 21
options.feedback: “Much longer” isn't the test. 400 + 441 = 841 = 29² exactly — right.

options.label: Acute — 841 < 400 + 441
options.feedback: Recompute: 400 + 441 = 841, which EQUALS 29² — equality means right, not acute.

options.label: Right — any odd-odd-odd side set is a triple
options.feedback: 20 is even, and no such parity rule exists. The real certificate: 400 + 441 = 841 = 29².

takeaways: Converse: a² + b² = c² certifies a right angle from side lengths alone.
c² < a² + b² → acute; c² > a² + b² → obtuse; equality → right.
Triples (3-4-5, 5-12-13, 8-15-17…) and their multiples are instant right triangles.
